summary: HF-DB-009-MARKETPLACE-TYPE-AND-RPC-SURFACE is actioned. Three additive forward-only migrations now carry the marketplace checkout money path, the external-listing redirect surface and a buyer-scoped entitlement download increment. Two of your three named objects are now IN the active chain, so they are captured rather than merely inventoried. Nothing was applied: CP-051 keeps the apply with the operator. Two decisions are yours, and one of them is a behavioural difference I could not resolve from the repository.
completed: marketplace_checkout_attempts: CAPTURED. 20260926120000 creates it with the archived 20260728000011 contract plus guest_email. The archived table has no guest_email, but app/api/marketplace/checkout/route.ts:467 writes it in the same upsert that claims the idempotency_key, so the archived DDL was behind the code. That is the only column added beyond the archive and it is caller-driven, not invented.

The same migration adds the six P6 guest-checkout columns to public.marketplace_orders (order_number, applied_fee_snapshot, idempotency_key, guest_email, guest_access_token, guest_access_token_expires_at) with three partial indexes. app/api/marketplace/checkout/route.ts:377-394 writes exactly these six. Without them the route's order insert fails after the attempts lookup is fixed, so the P0 was two columns deep, not one.

marketplace_external_listings: CAPTURED, together with marketplace_external_clicks and the four marketplace_listings columns the redirect route needs. 20260728000001's listing_kind/service_mode/public_slug/optimistic_version are required because app/api/marketplace/listings/[id]/redirect/route.ts:46 gates on listing_kind, and the embedded select at :36-42 needs the real FK the archived DDL already had.

marketplace_entitlements increment RPC: AUTHORED as public.record_marketplace_entitlement_download(uuid, text, timestamptz), SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned to public and EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and anon. It replaces the service-role compare-and-swap with one UPDATE whose WHERE clause carries buyer_user_id = auth.uid(), status = 'active' and download_count < max_downloads, so there is no read-modify-write window.

EXECUTED evidence, not static review: supabase/tests/db011_marketplace_surface.harness.sh runs the three migrations twice each on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster with the real chain migration 20260410120000_marketplace_core.sql applied verbatim, then asserts 33 checks including a real two-session concurrent race at the last remaining download credit. 33/33 pass. LOCAL EMULATION ONLY - not Supabase, not a hosted project, not a chain replay, no `supabase db reset`.

One deliberate narrowing of the archived DDL, flagged because it is the one place these files do not reproduce their source. 20260728000003 created a table-level public SELECT policy and a comment asserting canonical_url was excluded from it. A USING predicate cannot exclude a column, so that policy exposed the destination URL to any anonymous caller that satisfied the row predicate. It is replaced by a column-limited view public.marketplace_external_listings_public (listing_id, provider_name, provider_domain, safety_status) with the base table revoked from anon. This narrows access and cannot widen it, but the security-data reviewer must sign off on it because the archived design intended something it did not achieve.
next_steps: DECISION 1, yours, and it is behavioural: the function enforces `download_count < max_downloads` UNCONDITIONALLY. app/api/marketplace/delivery/[orderItemId]/route.ts currently applies `.lt('download_count', max_downloads)` only `if (entitlement.max_downloads > 0)`, which means your route treats 0 as unlimited and the new function does not. Either 0 is a real unlimited sentinel in your data model, in which case the function needs an explicit branch and the route's current reading is the bug, or 0 is unreachable, in which case the function is right as written. I could not decide this from the repository: the column is `max_downloads integer not null default 5` and no migration or seed writes 0. Answer this before the route is switched over.

DECISION 2, yours: switch app/api/marketplace/delivery/[orderItemId]/route.ts from `createServiceRoleClient()` to the AUTHENTICATED client when calling the new function. A service-role JWT carries no `sub` claim, so `auth.uid()` is null inside the function and every call would raise 42501. The migration is safe to apply before the code change (the old path is untouched), so ordering is yours. Once the route is switched, retire the SEC-109 `replace_with_rpc` reviewed-debt entry rather than renewing it.

REMAINING GAP, larger than the three objects this handoff named: 61 marketplace surface items from the 17 archived `local_only_unapplied` migrations are absent from the active chain AND have at least one product-code consumer. Only the checkout and external-listing subsets are closed here. Still open and still blocking their own routes: marketplace_payment_events, marketplace_fee_rules, marketplace_fulfillment_requests, marketplace_integration_products, marketplace_integration_sync_runs, marketplace_provider_webhook_events, marketplace_post_attachments, marketplace_service_requests, marketplace_service_offers, marketplace_service_bookings, marketplace_ticket_collections, and roughly 45 columns on marketplace_listings / marketplace_listing_variants / marketplace_integrations (integration_id, fulfillment_provider, fulfillment_profile, external_product_id, external_variant_id, source_provider, sync_status, last_external_synced_at, token_envelope, refresh_token_envelope, provider_scopes and others). Run `node supabase/tests/db011_marketplace_local_only_disposition.mjs .` for the machine-derived list. Recommend a second migration wave ordered by route criticality rather than by archive number.

AFTER the operator applies, regenerate lib/database.types.ts (CP-016). The gate that must pass first is `node supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs . <out> --check`, and it passes today: the chain is a strict superset of the contract, so regeneration can only add coverage.

FEEDBACK INTO THE MIGRATIONS: if your route tests reveal a column the four consumers need that the archived DDL does not have, send the exact column list rather than a type error. The Wave 33 refusal to invent a column contract still stands, and the one departure I did make (guest_email) came from a caller, not a guess.
